handbookNote: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR) boating safety and education program (dnr.sc.gov) and S.C. Code of Laws Title 50, Chapter 21 (motorboats and watercraft) -- South Carolina has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-95 requires individuals born on or after July 1, 2007 to pass an approved boater education course before operating a motorboat of 10 hp or more, a personal watercraft, or a specialty propcraft, with SCDNR approving courses under NASBLA, U.S. Coast Guard Auxiliary, and United States Power Squadrons standards -- in practice this means the NASBLA-approved course vendor's own embedded exam IS the de facto test, not a separate state exam, confirmed independently by two sources: SCDNR's own official boater education page (dnr.sc.gov/education/boated.html), which states the July 1, 2007 birth-date threshold and vessel/HP scope directly, and Boat-Ed's official South Carolina course (boat-ed.com/southcarolina), which independently confirms the same birth-date threshold and requires at least 70% on unit quizzes and at least 80% on the final certification exam with unlimited retake attempts (a passing-score convention matching this project's other Boat-Ed-based boating tracks); the exact final-exam question count is not consistently published by South Carolina's approved vendors and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted; a third source, the South Carolina Code of Laws itself (scstatehouse.gov/code/t50c021.php), independently corroborates the mandate's existence and scope while also grounding this track's South Carolina-specific statutory content: reckless operation and its statutory examples (Section 50-21-111), boating-under-the-influence with a materially-and-appreciably-impaired standard plus a three-tier BAC inference framework at 0.05%/0.08% (Sections 50-21-112 and 50-21-114(B)), personal watercraft rules including mandatory PFDs, the sunset-to-sunrise operating ban, and the engine cutoff lanyard requirement (Section 50-21-870), lake-specific idle-speed zones on Greenwood/Hartwell/Jocassee/Keowee/Marion and Lake Murray with an express Lake Moultrie exemption (Section 50-21-870(B)(6)), SCDNR's no-wake zone authority (Section 50-21-710), reportable-accident thresholds and the 48-hour reporting deadline (Sections 50-21-10(21) and 50-21-130(C)), SCDNR/Natural Resources Enforcement Division administrative and officer enforcement authority including a 2008 narrowing of stop-and-board language (Sections 50-21-40 and 50-21-80), water-ski observer/mirror and sunset-to-sunrise towing rules (Sections 50-21-810 and 50-21-820), and seasonal airboat restrictions near Lake Marion and the Santee Swamp (Section 50-21-860) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (PFD types, required federal equipment including fire extinguishers/ventilation/backfire flame control/visual distress signals, the Navigation Rules, the U.S. and Uniform State Aids to Navigation systems, cold-water immersion, and towed water sports safety) applied to South Carolina's major recreational lakes (Lake Murray, Lake Hartwell, Lake Marion) and its hurricane-exposed Atlantic coastline near Charleston and Myrtle Beach -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
